title: Secret bindings resolve through the secrets contract; no secret value ever lives in the manifest
asA: reviewer of a change that touches deploy config
iWant: certainty that a PR touching wrangler config cannot leak a secret
soThat: review moves as fast as the config change and nothing else

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every secret binding the Worker consumes at runtime is declared by NAME only in `wrangler.toml` (using the vendor's declaration primitive) and is populated on the deploy target through the vendor's own secret-set flow, sourced from the project's secrets contract.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project that has applied both this blueprint and the `security-secrets-management` blueprint (or an equivalent project-authored secrets contract)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the wrangler manifest is parsed and every secret binding it declares is cross-checked against the secrets contract's declared names
acceptanceCriteria.then: every secret binding named in the manifest maps to a name declared in the secrets contract; every name has a resolvable value in the active deploy environment; no binding declaration in the manifest carries an inline value

acceptanceCriteria.description: The CI workflows redact any log line that would emit a resolved secret value.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a CI run whose steps read a resolved secret value into a shell step that would echo it
acceptanceCriteria.when: the run's captured logs are inspected byte-for-byte after completion
acceptanceCriteria.then: no log line contains any byte sequence in the resolved-values set; every substitution shows a fixed placeholder in the emitted line

acceptanceCriteria.description: A committed file whose bytes match any resolved secret value is refused by the CI gate.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a change that adds a file whose contents include a byte sequence equal to any resolved secret value
acceptanceCriteria.when: the CI gate scans the change
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run fails with a stable-coded `DEPLOY_SECRET_LEAKED_IN_FILE` error naming the offending path and the logical name of the matching secret
